newsitem.title: GERMANY: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest - May 27.
newsitem.headline: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest - May 27.

text.p: REUTERS GERMAN ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the German press on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

FRANKFURT - Chemical group BASF is reconsidering representation for its seven-figure-budget corporate image campaign. Agencies Ogilvy & Mather of Frankfurt, Jung von Matt of Hamburg and current account holder Bozell of Frankfurt are considered top contenders. (Horizont)
WALLDORF - Werner Werbung of Hamburg will represent the ad account and public relations work of British charter airline Britannia Airways in Germany. (Kress)
FRANKFURT - News magazine Der Spiegel is returning to its former ad agency Springer & Jacoby to design its new television ad campaign. (Horizont)
FRANKFURT - Battery maker Ralston Energy System has signed on the Bates network for its Europe-wide ad account. (Horizont)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

FRANKFURT - More than 4.6 million adults are using online services in Germany, representing an increase of 33 percent over the previous year, according to the latest Niko-Advertising-Index. The research group measured use among Germans over 14 years old. (Horizont)
HAMBURG - Pay-TV television says it has selected a new marketing director, Gregory Gettinger. Gettinger will also be responsible for distribution, the channel says. (Reuter)
MUNICH - The radio programming directors of public network ARD plan to make deep cuts in foreign-language programming at their meeting on Wednesday. (Sueddeutsche Zeitung)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:
STUTTGART - Industrial group Daimler-Benz says the merger of its carmaker unit Mercedes-Benz AG into the parent company has been completed. (Reuter)

PARIS - German Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt says he could imagine Bonn taking further steps towards privatising Deutsche Telekom this year. Speaking on the sidelines of OECD ministerial talks in Paris, he did not give any further details of a possible further sale of shares drawn from Bonn's remaining 74 percent stake. (Reuter)

FRANKFURT - Tableware and bathroom fittings group Villeroy & Boch forecasts it will swing to profit in 1997 after orders and sales picked up in the first four months despite ongoing sluggish industry conditions. (Reuter)

DUESSELDORF - Textile groups Leffers AG and Sinn AG announce terms of their previously-announced merger. The companies say three Leffers shares, which have a nominal value of 50 marks ($29.52), will be exchanged for two Sinn shares, which also have a nominal value of 50 marks. (Reuter)
BONN - Foreign investment in German in the last year dropped to a record low of 1.1 billion marks last year (Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung)
PEOPLE NEWS:

HAMBURG - Publishing group Bauer Verlag says it has tapped Guenther Sell as a new member of its management board. Sell will focus on both advertising and marketing as well as activities in east Europe. (Reuter)
FRANKFURT - Barbara Roertgen will start soon as creative director for the international account of chemicals group Henkel with DDB Needham in Duesseldorf. (Horizont)
Deborah Cole, Berlin Newsroom, 49-30-203-98114
